summary: Host work for the next NAT-022 image `loader-diag-xnu-ckpt3`: the ADT boot-CPU reg fix (MPIDR & 0xffff), a compiled resumable C-checkpoint stub with a selectable stop list, a one-frame-per-pass report with a decoder, host tests against the NAT-033/035 instruction-level model, a mutation check, builds and RECOVERY packages for two stop lists (hashes only) and the draft text of the decision-0018 question. Nothing was flashed, run or sent to the phone; decision 0018 was not requested.

acceptance.1_adt_reg_patch: patch_loader3.py changes `adt_set_boot_cpu_mpidr(..., (uint32_t)gi.mpidr)` to `(uint32_t)(gi.mpidr & 0xffff)` with an exact-match replacement (base: NAT-020 build-003 loader source, GPL-2.0). test_nat036.py AdtMask compiles the patched expression, evaluates it for a raw MPIDR with bit 31 set, and feeds the value to the kernel's own ml_get_cpu_number_local() in the model: the patched ADT finds CPU 0; the loader as built does not (the NAT-035 finding).
acceptance.2_compiled_resumable_stub: ckpt3_stub.S + ckpt3.c compiled with the project toolchain (zig cc, the loader flags) run in the NAT-033/035 model on the real payload bytes: C3Chain (stops 1-5, the cp5 resume, 11,30-35,12) and C3LongChain (NAT036_LONG=1: all 17 stops, and the 9-stop candidate list 11,30,35,12,44,13,14,15,16, to checkpoint 16) end in the same kernel state, RAM and system registers as an uninterrupted run with every register the stub does not restore overwritten and tainted (no read of a clobbered register, DAIF masked at every entry). Negative controls on the compiled stub: each of the 13 restore/set-up instructions of the C tail replaced by a nop is detected; x18..x28 injected with distinct values come back; the frame layout; 81 textual mutants of the decision code, the stub and the report all killed on the final tests (six weak tests found by the mutation runs were strengthened and the mutants re-run).
